chunk_map.heading: How we work in this room

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 4 "How we work in this room": line 24: "Start from the same moves, then find your optimal way of working in your system." "the same moves" is never named anywhere in the file up to this point (checked chunk 0's blockquote, Big Idea, Prework, What You'll Learn) and is not resolved by any later slide either -- Start Here's exercise links come two slides later and are never labeled "moves." Grepped repo-wide for "the same moves": zero other hits, so it is not an arc-earned or cross-training phrase either. Harm: this is the room's first content slide after the LO list, read cold before any exercise has happened -- a reader has nothing to substitute for "the same moves" and the sentence resolves to noise rather than the intended point (do the shared exercises, then personalize).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name what's shared -- e.g. "start from the same exercises" or point at the arc ("the same loop") -- so the antecedent exists before it's leaned on.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No chunk points at another file by position. Chunk 6's eight links (lines 40-54) each name the target by title only ("Painting the picture with the LLM", "The machine you just met"), matching the navigational-pointer carve-out. Chunk 10 "Next" (line 86) names Module 2 by content ("where plan mode earns its keep"), not by file position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No "the X you did/saw/caught" construction appears anywhere in the body -- this is M1's own module file, the opening module, so there is no prior beat in this training to reference back to.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess/predict-then-reveal beat appears in this module file; it is a thin routing file (LOs, room agreement, link list, key concepts) with no live-demo narration.

Every chunk carries a self-standing claim or list: e.g. chunk 1 (line 6) states the Big Idea outright, chunk 5 (lines 30-34) is a standalone list of pacing choices, chunk 9 (lines 75-83) is a standalone reading list with its own annotations. None reduces to a bare wait-state bullet.

Checked each header against its chunk body: "How we work in this room" (line 22) is followed by three room-norm bullets that match; "Freedom to choose" (line 28) is followed by five pacing/discretion bullets that match; "Start here" (line 36) opens the room's opening question and the module's link list, which is literally where the room starts. No header is contradicted by its own content.

"Not X. Not Y. Z." construction: closest candidate is chunk 5 line 30 "Not too fast, not too slow" -- this is a paired-antonym clause inside one sentence, not the banned three-clause X/Y/Z pattern (no third declarative leg), so it stays inside. Anaphora/epistrophe triples: none found. Self-grading superlatives: none found (no "one of the most useful" or equivalent value-prop leak). Number + own retraction: no numbers stated and hedged in this file's body. Abstraction-noun stacks: none found. Verb triplets with an empty leg: none found.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Scanned body for repo/maintainer dialect (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun): none appear above the maintainer cut. "the loop" (first used chunk 7, line 57) is arc-earned spine vocabulary for this training, not repo dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 4 "How we work in this room": all three bullets open with a bolded lead sentence -- line 24 "**Make it work for you.**", line 25 "**Exercises.**", line 26 "**Everybody should be answering.**" -- the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture shape the rule bans ("every bullet on a slide opens with a bolded sentence"). This is not covered by the LO-template or task-sizing exceptions. Note: check_slides.md §9 itself names this exact slide as an open question it does not resolve ("Still genuinely open, not covered here: `## How we work in this room`'s bolded bullet leads, which no template mandates") -- flagging as a todo for the maintainer rather than asserting a settled violation, per the just-rewritten status of this chunk.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Flatten to a short bolded handle per bullet (≲5 words) or drop to plain-lead prose, per the standard budget -- or, if the pattern is deliberate here, add a maintainer accept-note and let the compendium's open question resolve.
